scope: Company. Florin Diumea personal brand remains separate.

strategy.headline: Decisions and accountability.
strategy.introduction: The place where owners and experts collaborate on the decisions that move the bottom line.
strategy.positioning: The place where owners and experts collaborate on the decisions that move the bottom line.

focus.name: Product
focus.line: A decision-making and accountability system for business owners and experts
focus.detail: Bright Business combines a working room, the Bright Business Operating System, the Human-Centred Matrix and continuing accountability. The Club brings the people together. BBOS maps the business. The Matrix structures a decision. Bright Brain supports the work between meetings.
focus.test: Each offer makes its role in the system clear.
rules_in: Real business decisions and accountable follow-through.
Peer advisory, expert judgment and a common operating method.
rules_out: A collection of talks presented as the whole product.
Software capabilities without a working demonstration.

focus.name: People
focus.line: Business owners building growth, value and exit readiness; experts building authority
focus.detail: Owners of established businesses, particularly those with $1M or more in revenue, need better decisions as they grow, transition or prepare to exit. Experts contribute one discipline in a room of owners and peers. Useful contribution builds authority, ambassadors and qualified warm introductions.
focus.test: Owner and expert invitations make their different value clear.
rules_in: Owners willing to work on a real business challenge.
Experts contributing specialist judgment, with one seat per discipline.
rules_out: Guaranteed leads or access to a prospecting list.
A general audience defined only by wanting success.

focus.name: Purpose
focus.detail: Bright Business exists to help members improve how they make decisions. Its founding belief is: “Businesses don’t fail. Decision-makers do.” That belief puts responsibility for judgment and action at the centre of the brand.
focus.test: Every activity improves a decision, its timing or the accountability that follows.
rules_in: Decision-making as a practice that can improve.
An owner who remains responsible for the decision.
rules_out: Community, learning or networking replacing the central purpose.
Activities with no connection to the business decision.

focus.name: Promise
focus.line: The best decision, at the best time, for the best outcome.
focus.detail: Better decisions serve growth, business value and exit readiness for owners. Experts build authority through contribution, then earn ambassadors and qualified warm leads. The promise directs the quality of the work; it does not guarantee a financial outcome.
focus.test: The recommendation explains why this decision, why now and what outcome it is intended to serve.
rules_in: Clear reasoning and honest statements of uncertainty.
rules_out: An estimate presented as an achieved result.

focus.name: Personality
focus.line: Direct. Calm. Honest about certainty. On the journey.
focus.detail: Name the diagnosis and its cost. Explain why the recommendation fits. State what is known and what still needs testing. Speak as a capable navigator accompanying an owner who makes the decision.
focus.test: The reader understands the issue, the reason and the next move.
rules_in: Plain language, specific diagnosis and reasons.
rules_out: Hype, generic praise and theatrical certainty.
A guru who claims to know the owner’s business better than the owner.

strategy.recommendation: Keep decisions and accountability at the centre. Show how the Club, BBOS, the Human-Centred Matrix and Bright Brain work together. Make the owner and expert value clear in their own invitations.

audiences.name: Business owners
audiences.need: The business has outgrown decisions made alone, late or from memory.
audiences.offer: A working session around a real constraint, with relevant peers and experts.

audiences.name: Experts
audiences.need: Good expertise needs to become visible through useful contributions.
audiences.offer: A focused place to teach, diagnose and contribute, with an ongoing role in the room.

persona.situation: An owner of an established business facing growth, transition or exit decisions.
persona.need: Relevant expertise, a structured decision process and follow-through.
persona.stakes: Growth, business value and readiness for the next stage.
persona.trigger: A consequential decision needs better judgment and accountability.

direction.title: Creative Direction
direction.job: Decisions and accountability, made visible through the Bright Business visual language.

sections.title: The visual world
sections.body: Paper and charcoal give the argument room. The red flag identifies the brand. Structure makes the decision legible; the Explorer makes the journey human.
sections.alt: Bright Business visual language with typography, palette, red flag, Explorer illustration and ten event compositions.

sections.title: Visual registers
rows: Geometry, clear type and purposeful data marks.
Frameworks, scorecards, decks and structured event invitations.
Charcoal ink, restrained watercolour and one red-shirt Explorer.
An idea, a journey or a working session made tangible.
The actual product screen, placed in a real context.
Product demonstrations supported by the interface that exists.

sections.title: Strategy and visual choices
rows: One dominant argument per surface. The hierarchy holds in grayscale.
Clear owner, action and follow-through in the content.
Generous paper, precise type and restrained colour.
The owner is the Explorer. The system provides the vehicle, path, compass, peers and navigator.

sections.title: Character and contrast
sections.body: Sage judgment leads the explanation. Structure, action and peer warmth support it. The visual balance changes with the job while the voice stays direct and calm.
rows: Use geometric structure to measure. Use the organic Explorer register to explain.
Give the argument space. Let a purposeful red mark carry the point of attention.
Explain the reasoning clearly, then make the business journey human.
Show the subject, the relationship and the next action. Avoid obscure decorative metaphors.

sections.title: Application examples
sections.body: Each composition keeps the same identity. The variation is in emphasis and arrangement.

visual-rules.title: Look and Feel
visual-rules.job: A practical specification for colour, type, composition and imagery.

sections.title: Pairings and legibility
rows: Default for all reading, small labels and numbers.
Use for a deliberate inverse field with generous spacing.
Brand flag; a diagnosed constraint; the Explorer’s shirt. Never generic emphasis.
The WHO / UX centre of the Human-Centred Matrix only.
No active role. Do not introduce it into assets.

sections.title: Typography
rows: Sentence case; tight but open; line height 1.05–1.12.
Short, legible and precise. Eyebrows uppercase only.
Never Spectral. No decorative number treatment.

sections.title: Composition
items: Start with one topic or decision. Make it the largest readable element.
Use a clear grid, six percent minimum safe margins and consistent alignment.
Group location and logistics; reserve a distinct place for partners and speakers.
Keep the brand mark smaller than the topic. Place it on an uncluttered field.
Cards may use a 25px radius; pills 40px; data marks remain square. Shadows belong only to cards.
Artwork has a fixed canvas. Scale it as a whole; never reflow a finished banner.

sections.title: Imagery
rows: Charcoal ink, loose pale sky and ground washes, one red-shirt protagonist. One understandable situation.
Use verified, suitable source photography. Preserve the person and the place.
Use an actual rendered screen. Never illustrate a fictional interface or member result.
Stock boardrooms, glossy pseudo-3D, decorative gradients, fabricated people presented as speakers.

sections.title: Do / avoid
sections.alt: Correct use of red flag, colour roles and text hierarchy beside examples of decorative colour and weak hierarchy.

sections.title: Accessible production
items: Use charcoal at full strength for small information. Low-opacity charcoal is for rules and nonessential marks.
Charcoal on paper exceeds 4.5:1. Red on paper is about 4:1, so do not use it for small body text.
Give interface controls visible keyboard focus and descriptive labels.
Write useful alt text for finished assets. Put event details in the accompanying text as well.
Keep text live in source masters; supply fixed PDF and PNG outputs.

logo.title: Logo
logo.job: One Bright Business shield across the ecosystem.

sections.title: The existing mark
sections.body: Use the supplied Bright Business artwork as one intact asset.

sections.title: Placement
items: Keep clear space of at least one shield-frame thickness, approximately 15.7% of shield width in the manual construction.
Preserve the complete aspect ratio and all lettering. Do not redraw, retype, stretch or recolour.
Use the available charcoal master on paper. On a charcoal composition, place the mark in a normal paper footer.
Program and location names are typeset labels, not new logos.
Use a licensed, supplied inverse master if one becomes available. Do not simulate one by filtering the charcoal asset.

sections.title: Partners
sections.body: Keep sponsor marks subordinate and separate from the Bright Business mark. Until an approved sponsor logo is supplied, typeset the sponsor name with its role. Kiln is the San Diego location sponsor; Serendipity Labs is the Costa Mesa location sponsor.

sections.title: The BBVL flag
sections.body: A red rectangle precedes the uppercase eyebrow. At the manual’s base size it is 30 × 8px, followed by an 11.5px bold label with 1.6px tracking. Scale the entire lockup together.

sections.title: Red flag usage
items: Use one flag to introduce the branded subject or series.
Keep the rectangle solid red and square-edged. No texture, gradient, rounding or animation.
Do not stretch it into a decorative stripe or repeat it beside every paragraph.
In the geometric register, additional red identifies a real constraint. In the illustration register, the Explorer’s shirt may carry red.
Maintain one identity across locations. A city never receives its own colour or mark.

sections.title: The Human-Centred Matrix
sections.body: This is Bright Business’s decision framework. Its orientation carries meaning.

sections.title: The decision sequence
items: Future State is north. Current State is south. How / PTP is west. What / ATP is east.
WHO / UX stays in the blue centre. Do not rotate or mirror the matrix.
Name the Weakest Link, then the Leverage Move. Show the formula last.
The matrix and the Brand Therapy Focus Star have different jobs. Do not combine their geometry or labels.

voice.title: Voice and Writing
voice.job: Direct. Calm. Honest about certainty. On the journey.

sections.title: Four principles
rows: Name the diagnosis, the cost and the next action. Use plain verbs.
Keep the sentence measured. Let the substance carry the urgency.
Distinguish what is known, estimated and still being tested. Explain why this recommendation.
Speak alongside the owner. The owner makes the decision; the room improves it.

sections.title: The core language
rows: The place where owners and experts collaborate on the decisions that move the bottom line.
The best decision, at the best time, for the best outcome.
One room. One system. One better decision, then the next.

sections.title: Company description
sections.body: Bright Business brings owners and experts together around decisions and accountability. Through the Club, the Bright Business Operating System, the Human-Centred Matrix and Bright Brain, members work on the decisions that support growth, business value and the next stage of their business.

sections.title: Five examples
rows: Every decision still comes back to you. That slows the business down. Identify which decisions someone else can own.
Start with the Current State. Define the Future State. Then decide what must change, how it will change and who owns the move.
A useful progress review names the original decision, the action taken and what happened.
Bring a business decision to the room. Work it through with owners and experts. Visit a meeting.
Thanks for the context. The first thing to clarify is who owns this decision. Once that is clear, we can work through the next move.

sections.title: Three corrections
rows: Work through the decision holding your business back.
Replace an abstract promise with a concrete task.
Join an amazing network of game-changers.
Owners and experts collaborating on real business decisions.
Name who is there and what they do.
Build authority through useful contributions to the room.
Do not turn an intended outcome into a guarantee.

sections.title: Terms and rhythm
items: Use Owner, Expert, Member and Club consistently. On owner pages, say owner rather than founder.
Use Weakest Link, Leverage Move, Matrix Movement, Destination and Machine when the underlying framework is relevant. Explain an unfamiliar term on first use.
Use Visit a meeting or Apply for a seat. Avoid generic join, sign up and register.
Address the reader as you. Give the diagnosis in one sentence, name its cost, then explain the recommendation.
Keep “You belong here” and “A society for business explorers” out of new company copy.
Use Stay Bright in notes from Florin or the Club; it need not close every asset.

personal-branding.title: Personal Branding
personal-branding.job: Bright Business is company-led and founder-endorsed.

sections.title: The relationship
sections.body: Florin Diumea contributes his experience, point of view and reputation. Bright Business owns the system, membership experience and event identity. Club leads and experts can carry that experience without turning every asset into a portrait of Florin.

sections.title: Use the right voice
rows: The system, member experience, programs, events and accountability.
A personal perspective, author’s explanation or founder’s message.
A named contribution to a specific session, shown with verified name and role.

sections.title: Character Sheet
sections.body: Not in use for this company system. Florin’s portrait, likeness and personal identity remain in his separate personal brand. Company event designs can work fully without a face.

overview.title: Applications
overview.job: Brand application across the four event programs.

sections.title: Event design concepts
sections.body: An illustrated world built around real business decisions, shared expertise and the next move. Each composition gives the Explorer a different role.
sections.alt: Ten Bright Business event designs across square, portrait, story and banner formats.

sections.title: One brand across four programs
sections.body: San Diego, Costa Mesa and Online share the Bright Business Club identity. The Marketing & Sales Group keeps its own program name within the same brand.

sections.title: Campaign formats
sections.body: A square starts the conversation. A story brings the idea closer. A cover identifies the event. A listing turns interest into attendance. Use the same visual idea across these formats, composing each for its setting.

sections.title: From calendar to finished assets
sections.body: Confirm the topic, date, time, venue and any speaker or sponsor details. The same identity rules govern the next invitation, the full monthly set and the August–July calendar.

sections.title: How the case study should prove its value
rows: Compare the original banners with the same four events using one identity.
Demonstrate a new event produced from its facts, with no manual layout work.
Record the time from confirmed brief to checked files. Compare with a real prior baseline.
Track qualified owner and expert inquiries, visits and membership progression over time. Attribute results cautiously.

events.title: Event design exploration
events.job: Ten illustrated event concepts across four social formats.

sections.title: From design to the next event
sections.body: These examples explore the visual direction. Add the confirmed topic, date, time, venue, speaker and sponsor details before using them for a scheduled event. The same idea can become a square post, story, cover and listing.

sections.title: Monthly and annual use
sections.body: Once a direction is selected, apply it across the four programs and the confirmed calendar. Each export follows the same brand rules while keeping the format and occasion in mind.

creative_exploration.brief: At least ten new image-led concepts, visibly different and presented together across event promotion formats.

workflow: Read strategy and identity, then the requested application.
Check required facts; ask only for missing information needed for the final asset.
Choose the appropriate composition and render the finished files.
Inspect output for hierarchy, typography, logo, signature, facts and clipping; fix issues and inspect again.
never: Change strategy to suit a design.
Invent dates, speakers, testimonials or results.
Generate a replacement logo or a real-person likeness.
Turn the deliverable into a client-operated template editor.
Send or publish without exact final-content approval.
